evidence: Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group: 'What did we do that is similar to what astronomers do?'
rationale: Three of four clauses are met. Students work with others to discuss topics: they respond to whole-group discussion prompts ("What did we do that is similar to what astronomers do?") and engage in turn-and-talk with elbow partners. Students work with others to investigate questions: in small presentation groups with visitors, "they will take turns answering questions from the visitors" using a Questions sheet. Students work with others to explore and create texts: they share their self-created "What the Sun Sees" poems and Sky notebooks in collaborative small groups. However, no activity has students work with others to solve problems — the lesson is a sharing/celebration lesson with no problem-solving component, so that clause is not met.
standard_raw_text: Work with others to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts. (I/C)
